articles.title: (W.E. Talk) Harold Weldon: Why does the Long March still resonate with the world today?
articles.titleCn: （W.E. Talk）哈罗德·韦尔登：长征为何至今仍能引起世界共鸣？
articles.summary: "The Long March is not only a Chinese story. It is also a universal story about how people persevere, cooperate and grow through adversity," Australian sinologist Harold Weldon said in a recent interview with  China News Service's "W.E. Talk".
articles.summaryCn: 澳大利亚汉学家哈罗德·韦尔登通过重走长征路、出版图书和跨文化交流，阐释长征超越意识形态的普遍人性价值，并见证中国减贫与发展成就。

paragraphs.en: "The Long March is not only a Chinese story. It is also a universal story about how people {{0}}, cooperate and grow through {{1}}," Australian {{2}} Harold Weldon said in a recent interview with China News Service's "W.E. Talk". Inspired by Red Star Over China, Weldon first retraced sections of the route taken by the Chinese Red Army during the Long March in 1985. He returned to the route in 2011 and participated in the publication of illustrated books including China: The Long March and China: The New Long March.
paragraphs.cn: “长征不仅是一个中国故事，也是一个关于人们如何在逆境中坚持、合作与成长的普遍故事，”澳大利亚汉学家哈罗德·韦尔登近日在接受中国新闻社“W.E. Talk”采访时表示。受《红星照耀中国》启发，韦尔登于1985年首次重走中国红军长征的部分路线。2011年他再次重返这条路线，并参与出版了《中国：长征》和《中国：新长征》等图文书。

paragraphs.en:
For more than four decades, Harold Weldon, Vice President of the Weldon International Group, has sought to introduce China to Western audiences through publishing, documentaries and cross-cultural projects. In his view, the story of the Long March continues to {{3}} beyond China because it {{4}} ideology and geopolitics and speaks to the shared human capacity to confront hardship with {{5}}, {{6}} and hope. Here are excerpts from the interview:
CNS: What led you to retrace the route of the Long March? Harold Weldon: My father first encountered Edgar Snow's Red Star Over China when he was at school in the early 1950s. Our family operated a privately owned publishing group, and around 1984 we were developing the concept for a book about China.
paragraphs.cn: 四十多年来，韦尔登国际集团副总裁哈罗德·韦尔登一直通过出版、纪录片和跨文化项目，努力向西方受众介绍中国。在他看来，长征的故事之所以能超越中国持续引发共鸣，是因为它超越了意识形态和地缘政治，触及了人类面对艰难困苦时以坚韧、团结和希望共同应对的共同能力。以下是采访摘录：中新社：是什么促使您重走长征路？哈罗德·韦尔登：我父亲在20世纪50年代初上学时第一次接触到埃德加·斯诺的《红星照耀中国》。我们家经营一家私营出版集团，大约在1984年，我们正在策划一本关于中国的书。

paragraphs.en: At that time, the Western world knew very little about China. Many people saw only rice paddies and rural scenes-a very small part of the country. My father suggested that the Long March, which was such an extraordinary story, could provide the narrative for a journey through China. By following its route, we could show Western readers the real China through the story of the Long March. I also first learned about the Long March at school, when we studied Red Star Over China.
paragraphs.cn: 当时，西方世界对中国知之甚少。许多人只看到稻田和乡村景象——那只是这个国家很小的一部分。我父亲提出，长征是如此非凡的故事，可以为一次穿越中国的旅程提供叙事主线。沿着长征路线，我们可以通过长征的故事向西方读者展示真实的中国。我也是在学校学习《红星照耀中国》时第一次了解到长征的。

paragraphs.en: Later, I came to understand that Edgar Snow's wife, Helen Snow, also played an {{7}} role. She conducted important interviews and travelled to the revolutionary base areas. Years later, I visited the Snows' former residence in Beijing. My father and I were both deeply inspired by Red Star Over China and the vivid way in which it brought the Long March to international readers. CNS: What motivated you to tell the story of the Long March to an international audience?
paragraphs.cn: 后来，我逐渐了解到埃德加·斯诺的妻子海伦·斯诺也发挥了重要作用。她进行了重要的采访，并前往革命根据地。多年后，我参观了斯诺夫妇在北京的故居。我和父亲都深受《红星照耀中国》的启发，它生动地将长征带给了国际读者。中新社：是什么促使您向国际受众讲述长征的故事？

paragraphs.en: Harold Weldon: The Long March is one of the greatest examples of human {{8}} and perseverance in world history. It is a remarkable historical story in its own right, but it also gave us an opportunity to place that history alongside the China of the 1980s. In the illustrated book we produced, roughly half was devoted to the historical narrative. For the other half, photographers from around the world were assigned to different sections of the Long March route. Readers could learn what had happened there historically while also seeing what those places and their people looked like in a modern context.
paragraphs.cn: 哈罗德·韦尔登：长征是世界历史上人类忍耐力和毅力最伟大的典范之一。它本身就是一个非凡的历史故事，但它也给了我们一个机会，将那段历史与20世纪80年代的中国并置呈现。在我们制作的图文书里，大约一半篇幅用于历史叙事。另一半则安排来自世界各地的摄影师前往长征路线的不同路段。读者可以了解那里历史上发生过什么，同时也能看到那些地方和那里的人们在现代背景下的面貌。

paragraphs.en: The book therefore told several stories at once: a universal story of endurance and achievement, a story about China's development, and a story about the lives of ordinary Chinese people. We encountered people from different ethnic groups and saw the extraordinary {{9}} of China's landscape-from mountains and forests to deserts and raging rivers. All of this went far beyond what many Western readers at the time knew or imagined about China. CNS: How did retracing the Long March shape your understanding of China? Harold Weldon: The Long March taught me something deeper than simply triumphing over adversity.
paragraphs.cn: 因此，这本书同时讲述了几个故事：一个关于忍耐与成就的普遍故事，一个关于中国发展的故事，以及一个关于中国普通百姓生活的故事。我们遇到了不同民族的人，看到了中国地貌的非凡多样性——从高山森林到沙漠和湍急的河流。所有这些都远远超出了当时许多西方读者对中国的了解或想象。中新社：重走长征路如何塑造了您对中国的理解？哈罗德·韦尔登：长征教给我的东西比单纯战胜逆境更深刻。

paragraphs.en: It taught me that it is through adversity that we can become better people. We often think that success means defeating a hardship or emerging victorious from a struggle. But what the Red Army experienced-and we experienced only a tiny fraction of it-teaches another lesson: people must work together, share a common purpose, refuse to give up and make sure that the person beside them is all right. A journey like that cannot be completed as an individual pursuit without concern for others. It taught me resilience, solidarity and the importance of looking after one another.
paragraphs.cn: 它教会我，正是通过逆境，我们才能成为更好的人。我们常常认为成功意味着战胜困难或从斗争中胜利走出。但红军所经历的——而我们只经历了其中极小的一部分——教给我们另一个道理：人们必须共同努力，怀有共同的目标，绝不放弃，并确保身边的人安然无恙。这样的旅程不可能作为个人追求而完成，而不顾及他人。它教会了我坚韧、团结以及相互关照的重要性。

paragraphs.en: The journey also introduced me to a China beyond politics and major cities. In the countryside, we met villagers who possessed very little but welcomed us into their homes and offered us the best food they had. I once admired a picture hanging on the wall of a village home, and the family immediately wanted to give it to me. At first, I did not know how to respond. I later understood that this generosity reflected a traditional Chinese culture of giving and {{19}}.
paragraphs.cn: 这段旅程还让我认识了一个超越政治和大城市的中国。在乡村，我们遇到了一些拥有很少却欢迎我们到家中、把最好的食物拿出来招待我们的村民。我曾称赞一幅挂在村民家中墙上的画，那家人立刻就想把它送给我。起初，我不知道该如何回应。后来我明白，这种慷慨反映了中国传统的给予和好客文化。

paragraphs.en: Today, the internet gives us access to an enormous amount of information. Yet our understanding can still be narrow. A firsthand visit makes an enormous difference. I sincerely hope that more Australians will have the opportunity to visit China and see the country for themselves. CNS: You've visited China many times.
paragraphs.cn: 如今，互联网让我们能够获取大量信息。然而我们的理解仍可能很狭隘。亲身走访会带来巨大不同。我真诚希望更多澳大利亚人有机会访问中国，亲眼看看这个国家。中新社：您多次访问中国。

paragraphs.en: What changes have you witnessed, and what has felt different at different stages? Harold Weldon: I think the major change is the overall {{10}} of poverty, the lifting of the Chinese people out of poverty and out of a lower standard of living. I have seen it with my own eyes, with my feet walking. It's been incredible. The best example was Hongyuan, up in the grasslands.
paragraphs.cn: 您目睹了哪些变化，不同阶段有什么不同感受？哈罗德·韦尔登：我认为主要变化是整体脱贫，中国人民摆脱了贫困，摆脱了较低的生活水平。我亲眼所见，双脚走过。这令人难以置信。最好的例子是草原上的红原。

paragraphs.en: In 1985, it was very remote. There were cabbages and watermelons-a watermelon in the summer, a cabbage in the winter. Then, when we went back in 2011, there was every variety of fruit and vegetable that had come, probably from Guangdong or somewhere, because the roads had improved, and rail and trade had improved. Now, this time, in Hongyuan in 2026, there's a convenience store with everything you would find in Beijing or Shanghai-all of the small toys and all of the conveniences-because the road system is so brilliant. While still retaining the traditional life, I think it's really important for China to embrace the new but hold on to those traditions.
paragraphs.cn: 1985年，那里非常偏远。只有白菜和西瓜——夏天吃西瓜，冬天吃白菜。后来，2011年我们回去时，各种水果蔬菜都有了，可能来自广东或其他地方，因为道路改善了，铁路和贸易也改善了。现在，2026年这次在红原，有一家便利店，里面有你在北京或上海能找到的一切——所有小玩具和所有便利品——因为道路系统太棒了。在保留传统生活的同时，我认为中国拥抱新事物并坚守那些传统非常重要。

paragraphs.en: Because once those traditions are lost, everything becomes the same. Somewhere like Hongyuan, there is still the local culture, and the local cowboys with the yaks, herding the yaks. But still, everyone has a right to have a better life. So that's a summary of the alleviation of poverty, and the {{11}} all runs behind that. The quality of life has improved, especially through infrastructure, with a good balance of traditional life and modern life.
paragraphs.cn: 因为一旦那些传统丢失，一切都会变得千篇一律。像红原这样的地方，仍有当地文化，还有放牧牦牛的当地牛仔。但尽管如此，每个人都有权过上更好的生活。所以这就是减贫的概括，基础设施都随之发展。生活质量提高了，尤其是通过基础设施，传统生活与现代生活之间保持了良好平衡。

paragraphs.en: CNS: Having revisited places along the Long March route several times, what changes have impressed you most? Harold Weldon: What has impressed me most is China's achievement in reducing poverty. People have emerged from poverty, and their living standards have continued to improve. These are changes I have witnessed firsthand on my journeys, and they have been remarkable. Hongyuan in Sichuan is a clear example.
paragraphs.cn: 中新社：多次重访长征路线沿途地方后，哪些变化给您印象最深？哈罗德·韦尔登：给我印象最深的是中国在减贫方面的成就。人们摆脱了贫困，生活水平持续提高。这些是我在旅途中亲眼目睹的变化，非常了不起。四川红原就是一个明显的例子。

paragraphs.en: When I first visited in 1985, it was still quite remote, and the selection of fruit and vegetables was very limited. When we returned in 2011, we found a wide variety of fresh produce. Behind this change were better roads and improvements in rail transport and trade. Returning to Hongyuan this year, I found the local convenience stores stocked with a much wider range of goods. From small toys to everyday essentials, things you could buy in Beijing or Shanghai were available there too.
paragraphs.cn: 1985年我第一次去时，那里还相当偏远，水果蔬菜的选择非常有限。2011年我们回去时，发现了种类丰富的新鲜农产品。这一变化的背后是更好的道路以及铁路运输和贸易的改善。今年回到红原，我发现当地便利店备有种类多得多的商品。从小玩具到日常必需品，在北京或上海能买到的东西那里也有。

paragraphs.en:
A well-developed road network has made daily life more convenient. At the same time, the area has retained its traditional culture and {{12}} way of life, maintaining a good balance between tradition and modern life. CNS: This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Why does its story continue to resonate around the world? Weldon: I believe many countries have experienced their own "Long March moments."
In Australia, one example is the ANZAC spirit associated with the Gallipoli campaign.
paragraphs.cn: 发达的道路网络让日常生活更加便利。与此同时，该地区保留了传统文化和牧区生活方式，在传统与现代生活之间保持了良好平衡。中新社：今年是长征胜利90周年。为什么长征的故事继续在世界各地引起共鸣？韦尔登：我相信许多国家都经历过自己的“长征时刻”。在澳大利亚，一个例子是与加里波利战役相关的澳新军团精神。

paragraphs.en: In purely military terms, the campaign was a defeat. Yet Australians continue to {{13}} the courage of the soldiers, their refusal to give up in extremely difficult circumstances and their commitment to looking after their mates. That spirit has something in common with the spirit of the Long March. There is another parallel in American history: the Continental Army's winter encampment at Valley Forge during the American Revolutionary War. George Washington's army endured bitter cold, hunger, disease and repeated setbacks.
paragraphs.cn: 从纯军事角度看，那场战役是一场失败。然而澳大利亚人继续纪念士兵们的勇气、他们在极其困难的情况下绝不放弃的精神以及他们照顾战友的承诺。这种精神与长征精神有共同之处。美国历史上还有另一个相似之处：美国独立战争期间大陆军在福吉谷的冬季营地。乔治·华盛顿的军队忍受了严寒、饥饿、疾病和反复的挫折。

paragraphs.en: It came close to {{14}}. If that winter had destroyed Washington's army, the course of American history might have been entirely different. There are many such historical parallels. What people everywhere can understand is a story of surviving against overwhelming odds. It is the story of people continuing when success appears impossible.
paragraphs.cn: 它几乎瓦解。如果那个冬天摧毁了华盛顿的军队，美国历史的进程可能会完全不同。有许多这样的历史相似之处。各地人们都能理解的是一个在压倒性劣势中幸存下来的故事。这是人们在成功似乎不可能时继续前行的故事。

paragraphs.en: Different interpretations of the Long March may emerge over time, but the historical fact remains: people endured an extraordinary {{15}}, and what they accomplished shaped China's future. Even 90 years later, I still find the Long March inspiring. The resilience, unity and hope it represents are not confined to one country. They are part of humanity's shared spiritual heritage. In that sense, every country has its own Long March.
paragraphs.cn: 随着时间推移，对长征可能会有不同的解读，但历史事实依然存在：人们经历了非凡的磨难，他们所取得的成就塑造了中国的未来。即使在90年后，我仍然觉得长征令人鼓舞。它所代表的坚韧、团结和希望并不局限于一个国家。它们是人类共同精神遗产的一部分。从这个意义上说，每个国家都有自己的长征。

paragraphs.en: CNS: You have spent many years working in cross-cultural communication. At what level do Chinese and Australian people connect most strongly? Weldon: What resonates most strongly is usually something personal and connected to everyday life. An Australian family wants life to be better for its children. A Chinese family wants exactly the same thing.
paragraphs.cn: 中新社：您多年从事跨文化交流。中澳两国人民在哪个层面最能产生共鸣？韦尔登：最能引起共鸣的通常是个人化的、与日常生活相关的事情。一个澳大利亚家庭希望自己的孩子生活得更好。一个中国家庭想要的完全一样。

paragraphs.en: There is no geopolitics in that. It is a shared human {{16}}. I was involved in a photographic project called A Day in the Life of China. Nearly 100 photographers from around the world were sent to different locations across China to document a single day. The book began at midnight and ended at midnight.
paragraphs.cn: 那里没有地缘政治。这是一种共同的人类愿望。我参与了一个名为《中国一日》的摄影项目。来自世界各地的近100名摄影师被派往中国各地，记录同一天。这本书从午夜开始，到午夜结束。

paragraphs.en: Readers could see a farmer waking in a wheat field at dawn, a street vendor working in a city or a fashion model taking part in a photo shoot in Shanghai. When these scenes are placed together, people recognise how much they have in common, wherever they live. News coverage often concentrates on geopolitics, conflict, fear and uncertainty. But mutual understanding and trust are built through the real lives of ordinary people. That is why community-level and family-level connections matter so much.
paragraphs.cn: 读者可以看到农民在黎明时在小麦地里醒来，街头小贩在城市里工作，或者时装模特在上海参加拍摄。当这些场景放在一起时，人们会认识到，无论住在哪里，他们都有很多共同点。新闻报道往往集中于地缘政治、冲突、恐惧和不确定性。但相互理解和信任是通过普通人的真实生活建立起来的。这就是为什么社区层面和家庭层面的联系如此重要。

paragraphs.en: People-to-people exchange must also move beyond slogans. It is not simply about watching a tai chi demonstration or a dragon dance. It means people working together, sharing meals, making music, studying and creating things together. Cultural exchange becomes meaningful when people genuinely participate in one another's lives. CNS: Apart from the Long March, what other stories about China interest you?
paragraphs.cn: 人文交流也必须超越口号。它不仅仅是观看太极拳表演或舞龙。它意味着人们一起工作、一起吃饭、一起做音乐、一起学习和创造。当人们真正参与彼此的生活时，文化交流才有意义。中新社：除了长征，您还对中国的哪些故事感兴趣？

paragraphs.en: Weldon: I have always been interested in Chinese innovation. Some people in the West once regarded China simply as a "copycat," but I have never agreed with that view. China has produced important inventions throughout its history. Today, it is demonstrating strong innovative capacity in areas such as electric vehicles and artificial intelligence. I would like to see more stories about that innovation reach international audiences.
paragraphs.cn: 韦尔登：我一直对中国的创新感兴趣。西方有些人曾把中国仅仅视为“模仿者”，但我从未同意这种观点。中国历史上产生过重要发明。今天，中国在电动汽车和人工智能等领域展现出强大的创新能力。我希望更多关于这种创新的故事能传达给国际受众。

paragraphs.en: At the same time, cultural projects remain my greatest interest. I am particularly interested in three kinds of cross-cultural stories. The first concerns Australians in China. One example is George Ernest Morrison, the Australian journalist known as "Morrison of Peking." The second concerns Chinese people in Australia. The history of Chinese migrants during the gold rush contains many remarkable stories.
paragraphs.cn: 与此同时，文化项目仍然是我最大的兴趣。我对三种跨文化故事特别感兴趣。第一种是关于在中国的澳大利亚人。一个例子是乔治·欧内斯特·莫理循，这位澳大利亚记者被称为“北京的莫理循”。第二种是关于在澳大利亚的中国人。淘金热时期中国移民的历史包含许多非凡的故事。

paragraphs.en: The third area is the everyday reality of Australian society. I would like Chinese audiences to see more informative and {{17}} stories about how Australians actually live. Many of these cross-cultural stories have yet to be fully told. I hope to continue serving as a bridge, helping Australians and Chinese see a more {{18}}, complex and human side of one another. (End)n is an Australian sinologist, documentary producer, writer, presenter, and photographer with 41 years of experience in Australia-China cultural media and bilateral relations.
paragraphs.cn: 第三个领域是澳大利亚社会的日常现实。我希望中国受众看到更多关于澳大利亚人实际生活方式的、信息丰富且细致入微的故事。这些跨文化故事中有许多尚未被充分讲述。我希望继续充当桥梁，帮助澳大利亚人和中国人看到彼此更真实、更复杂、更人性化的一面。（完）他是一位澳大利亚汉学家、纪录片制片人、作家、主持人和摄影师，在澳中文化媒体和双边关系方面拥有41年经验。

paragraphs.en: He is a Special Advisor on China affairs, a recipient of a Peabody Award and China's National level Golden Book Award, and a former member of the Australia China Council.
paragraphs.cn: 他是中国事务特别顾问，曾获皮博迪奖和中国国家图书奖，并曾是澳中理事会成员。

articles.fullText:
"The Long March is not only a Chinese story. It is also a universal story about how people persevere, cooperate and grow through adversity," Australian sinologist Harold Weldon said in a recent interview with China News Service's "W.E. Talk".
Inspired by Red Star Over China, Weldon first retraced sections of the route taken by the Chinese Red Army during the Long March in 1985. He returned to the route in 2011 and participated in the publication of illustrated books including China: The Long March and China: The New Long March.
For more than four decades, Harold Weldon, Vice President of the Weldon International Group, has sought to introduce China to Western audiences through publishing, documentaries and cross-cultural projects.
In his view, the story of the Long March continues to resonate beyond China because it transcends ideology and geopolitics and speaks to the shared human capacity to confront hardship with resilience, solidarity and hope.
Here are excerpts from the interview:
CNS: What led you to retrace the route of the Long March?
Harold Weldon: My father first encountered Edgar Snow's Red Star Over China when he was at school in the early 1950s. Our family operated a privately owned publishing group, and around 1984 we were developing the concept for a book about China.
At that time, the Western world knew very little about China. Many people saw only rice paddies and rural scenes-a very small part of the country. My father suggested that the Long March, which was such an extraordinary story, could provide the narrative for a journey through China. By following its route, we could show Western readers the real China through the story of the Long March.
I also first learned about the Long March at school, when we studied Red Star Over China. Later, I came to understand that Edgar Snow's wife, Helen Snow, also played an instrumental role. She conducted important interviews and travelled to the revolutionary base areas. Years later, I visited the Snows' former residence in Beijing.
My father and I were both deeply inspired by Red Star Over China and the vivid way in which it brought the Long March to international readers.
CNS: What motivated you to tell the story of the Long March to an international audience?
Harold Weldon: The Long March is one of the greatest examples of human endurance and perseverance in world history. It is a remarkable historical story in its own right, but it also gave us an opportunity to place that history alongside the China of the 1980s.
In the illustrated book we produced, roughly half was devoted to the historical narrative. For the other half, photographers from around the world were assigned to different sections of the Long March route.
Readers could learn what had happened there historically while also seeing what those places and their people looked like in a modern context. The book therefore told several stories at once: a universal story of endurance and achievement, a story about China's development, and a story about the lives of ordinary Chinese people.
We encountered people from different ethnic groups and saw the extraordinary diversity of China's landscape-from mountains and forests to deserts and raging rivers.
All of this went far beyond what many Western readers at the time knew or imagined about China.
CNS: How did retracing the Long March shape your understanding of China?
Harold Weldon: The Long March taught me something deeper than simply triumphing over adversity. It taught me that it is through adversity that we can become better people.
We often think that success means defeating a hardship or emerging victorious from a struggle. But what the Red Army experienced-and we experienced only a tiny fraction of it-teaches another lesson: people must work together, share a common purpose, refuse to give up and make sure that the person beside them is all right.
A journey like that cannot be completed as an individual pursuit without concern for others. It taught me resilience, solidarity and the importance of looking after one another.
The journey also introduced me to a China beyond politics and major cities. In the countryside, we met villagers who possessed very little but welcomed us into their homes and offered us the best food they had.
I once admired a picture hanging on the wall of a village home, and the family immediately wanted to give it to me. At first, I did not know how to respond. I later understood that this generosity reflected a traditional Chinese culture of giving and hospitality.
Today, the internet gives us access to an enormous amount of information. Yet our understanding can still be narrow. A firsthand visit makes an enormous difference. I sincerely hope that more Australians will have the opportunity to visit China and see the country for themselves.
CNS: You've visited China many times. What changes have you witnessed, and what has felt different at different stages?
Harold Weldon: I think the major change is the overall alleviation of poverty, the lifting of the Chinese people out of poverty and out of a lower standard of living. I have seen it with my own eyes, with my feet walking. It's been incredible.
The best example was Hongyuan, up in the grasslands. In 1985, it was very remote. There were cabbages and watermelons-a watermelon in the summer, a cabbage in the winter. Then, when we went back in 2011, there was every variety of fruit and vegetable that had come, probably from Guangdong or somewhere, because the roads had improved, and rail and trade had improved.
Now, this time, in Hongyuan in 2026, there's a convenience store with everything you would find in Beijing or Shanghai-all of the small toys and all of the conveniences-because the road system is so brilliant.
While still retaining the traditional life, I think it's really important for China to embrace the new but hold on to those traditions. Because once those traditions are lost, everything becomes the same. Somewhere like Hongyuan, there is still the local culture, and the local cowboys with the yaks, herding the yaks.
But still, everyone has a right to have a better life. So that's a summary of the alleviation of poverty, and the infrastructure all runs behind that. The quality of life has improved, especially through infrastructure, with a good balance of traditional life and modern life.
CNS: Having revisited places along the Long March route several times, what changes have impressed you most?
Harold Weldon: What has impressed me most is China's achievement in reducing poverty. People have emerged from poverty, and their living standards have continued to improve. These are changes I have witnessed firsthand on my journeys, and they have been remarkable.
Hongyuan in Sichuan is a clear example. When I first visited in 1985, it was still quite remote, and the selection of fruit and vegetables was very limited. When we returned in 2011, we found a wide variety of fresh produce. Behind this change were better roads and improvements in rail transport and trade.
Returning to Hongyuan this year, I found the local convenience stores stocked with a much wider range of goods. From small toys to everyday essentials, things you could buy in Beijing or Shanghai were available there too. A well-developed road network has made daily life more convenient. At the same time, the area has retained its traditional culture and pastoral way of life, maintaining a good balance between tradition and modern life.
CNS: This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Why does its story continue to resonate around the world?
Weldon: I believe many countries have experienced their own "Long March moments."
In Australia, one example is the ANZAC spirit associated with the Gallipoli campaign. In purely military terms, the campaign was a defeat. Yet Australians continue to commemorate the courage of the soldiers, their refusal to give up in extremely difficult circumstances and their commitment to looking after their mates.
That spirit has something in common with the spirit of the Long March.
There is another parallel in American history: the Continental Army's winter encampment at Valley Forge during the American Revolutionary War. George Washington's army endured bitter cold, hunger, disease and repeated setbacks. It came close to disintegration.
If that winter had destroyed Washington's army, the course of American history might have been entirely different.
There are many such historical parallels. What people everywhere can understand is a story of surviving against overwhelming odds. It is the story of people continuing when success appears impossible.
Different interpretations of the Long March may emerge over time, but the historical fact remains: people endured an extraordinary ordeal, and what they accomplished shaped China's future.
Even 90 years later, I still find the Long March inspiring. The resilience, unity and hope it represents are not confined to one country. They are part of humanity's shared spiritual heritage. In that sense, every country has its own Long March.
CNS: You have spent many years working in cross-cultural communication. At what level do Chinese and Australian people connect most strongly?
Weldon: What resonates most strongly is usually something personal and connected to everyday life.
An Australian family wants life to be better for its children. A Chinese family wants exactly the same thing. There is no geopolitics in that. It is a shared human aspiration.
I was involved in a photographic project called A Day in the Life of China. Nearly 100 photographers from around the world were sent to different locations across China to document a single day.
The book began at midnight and ended at midnight. Readers could see a farmer waking in a wheat field at dawn, a street vendor working in a city or a fashion model taking part in a photo shoot in Shanghai.
When these scenes are placed together, people recognise how much they have in common, wherever they live.
News coverage often concentrates on geopolitics, conflict, fear and uncertainty. But mutual understanding and trust are built through the real lives of ordinary people. That is why community-level and family-level connections matter so much.
People-to-people exchange must also move beyond slogans. It is not simply about watching a tai chi demonstration or a dragon dance. It means people working together, sharing meals, making music, studying and creating things together. Cultural exchange becomes meaningful when people genuinely participate in one another's lives.
CNS: Apart from the Long March, what other stories about China interest you?
Weldon: I have always been interested in Chinese innovation. Some people in the West once regarded China simply as a "copycat," but I have never agreed with that view.
China has produced important inventions throughout its history. Today, it is demonstrating strong innovative capacity in areas such as electric vehicles and artificial intelligence. I would like to see more stories about that innovation reach international audiences.
At the same time, cultural projects remain my greatest interest. I am particularly interested in three kinds of cross-cultural stories. The first concerns Australians in China. One example is George Ernest Morrison, the Australian journalist known as "Morrison of Peking." The second concerns Chinese people in Australia. The history of Chinese migrants during the gold rush contains many remarkable stories. The third area is the everyday reality of Australian society. I would like Chinese audiences to see more informative and nuanced stories about how Australians actually live.
Many of these cross-cultural stories have yet to be fully told. I hope to continue serving as a bridge, helping Australians and Chinese see a more authentic, complex and human side of one another. (End)n is an Australian sinologist, documentary producer, writer, presenter, and photographer with 41 years of experience in Australia-China cultural media and bilateral relations. He is a Special Advisor on China affairs, a recipient of a Peabody Award and China's National level Golden Book Award, and a former member of the Australia China Council.

“长征不仅是一个中国故事，也是一个关于人们如何在逆境中坚持、合作与成长的普遍故事，”澳大利亚汉学家哈罗德·韦尔登近日在接受中国新闻社“W.E. Talk”采访时表示。受《红星照耀中国》启发，韦尔登于1985年首次重走中国红军长征的部分路线。2011年他再次重返这条路线，并参与出版了《中国：长征》和《中国：新长征》等图文书。

四十多年来，韦尔登国际集团副总裁哈罗德·韦尔登一直通过出版、纪录片和跨文化项目，努力向西方受众介绍中国。在他看来，长征的故事之所以能超越中国持续引发共鸣，是因为它超越了意识形态和地缘政治，触及了人类面对艰难困苦时以坚韧、团结和希望共同应对的共同能力。以下是采访摘录：中新社：是什么促使您重走长征路？哈罗德·韦尔登：我父亲在20世纪50年代初上学时第一次接触到埃德加·斯诺的《红星照耀中国》。我们家经营一家私营出版集团，大约在1984年，我们正在策划一本关于中国的书。

当时，西方世界对中国知之甚少。许多人只看到稻田和乡村景象——那只是这个国家很小的一部分。我父亲提出，长征是如此非凡的故事，可以为一次穿越中国的旅程提供叙事主线。沿着长征路线，我们可以通过长征的故事向西方读者展示真实的中国。我也是在学校学习《红星照耀中国》时第一次了解到长征的。

后来，我逐渐了解到埃德加·斯诺的妻子海伦·斯诺也发挥了重要作用。她进行了重要的采访，并前往革命根据地。多年后，我参观了斯诺夫妇在北京的故居。我和父亲都深受《红星照耀中国》的启发，它生动地将长征带给了国际读者。中新社：是什么促使您向国际受众讲述长征的故事？

哈罗德·韦尔登：长征是世界历史上人类忍耐力和毅力最伟大的典范之一。它本身就是一个非凡的历史故事，但它也给了我们一个机会，将那段历史与20世纪80年代的中国并置呈现。在我们制作的图文书里，大约一半篇幅用于历史叙事。另一半则安排来自世界各地的摄影师前往长征路线的不同路段。读者可以了解那里历史上发生过什么，同时也能看到那些地方和那里的人们在现代背景下的面貌。

因此，这本书同时讲述了几个故事：一个关于忍耐与成就的普遍故事，一个关于中国发展的故事，以及一个关于中国普通百姓生活的故事。我们遇到了不同民族的人，看到了中国地貌的非凡多样性——从高山森林到沙漠和湍急的河流。所有这些都远远超出了当时许多西方读者对中国的了解或想象。中新社：重走长征路如何塑造了您对中国的理解？哈罗德·韦尔登：长征教给我的东西比单纯战胜逆境更深刻。

它教会我，正是通过逆境，我们才能成为更好的人。我们常常认为成功意味着战胜困难或从斗争中胜利走出。但红军所经历的——而我们只经历了其中极小的一部分——教给我们另一个道理：人们必须共同努力，怀有共同的目标，绝不放弃，并确保身边的人安然无恙。这样的旅程不可能作为个人追求而完成，而不顾及他人。它教会了我坚韧、团结以及相互关照的重要性。

这段旅程还让我认识了一个超越政治和大城市的中国。在乡村，我们遇到了一些拥有很少却欢迎我们到家中、把最好的食物拿出来招待我们的村民。我曾称赞一幅挂在村民家中墙上的画，那家人立刻就想把它送给我。起初，我不知道该如何回应。后来我明白，这种慷慨反映了中国传统的给予和好客文化。

如今，互联网让我们能够获取大量信息。然而我们的理解仍可能很狭隘。亲身走访会带来巨大不同。我真诚希望更多澳大利亚人有机会访问中国，亲眼看看这个国家。中新社：您多次访问中国。

您目睹了哪些变化，不同阶段有什么不同感受？哈罗德·韦尔登：我认为主要变化是整体脱贫，中国人民摆脱了贫困，摆脱了较低的生活水平。我亲眼所见，双脚走过。这令人难以置信。最好的例子是草原上的红原。

1985年，那里非常偏远。只有白菜和西瓜——夏天吃西瓜，冬天吃白菜。后来，2011年我们回去时，各种水果蔬菜都有了，可能来自广东或其他地方，因为道路改善了，铁路和贸易也改善了。现在，2026年这次在红原，有一家便利店，里面有你在北京或上海能找到的一切——所有小玩具和所有便利品——因为道路系统太棒了。在保留传统生活的同时，我认为中国拥抱新事物并坚守那些传统非常重要。

因为一旦那些传统丢失，一切都会变得千篇一律。像红原这样的地方，仍有当地文化，还有放牧牦牛的当地牛仔。但尽管如此，每个人都有权过上更好的生活。所以这就是减贫的概括，基础设施都随之发展。生活质量提高了，尤其是通过基础设施，传统生活与现代生活之间保持了良好平衡。

中新社：多次重访长征路线沿途地方后，哪些变化给您印象最深？哈罗德·韦尔登：给我印象最深的是中国在减贫方面的成就。人们摆脱了贫困，生活水平持续提高。这些是我在旅途中亲眼目睹的变化，非常了不起。四川红原就是一个明显的例子。

1985年我第一次去时，那里还相当偏远，水果蔬菜的选择非常有限。2011年我们回去时，发现了种类丰富的新鲜农产品。这一变化的背后是更好的道路以及铁路运输和贸易的改善。今年回到红原，我发现当地便利店备有种类多得多的商品。从小玩具到日常必需品，在北京或上海能买到的东西那里也有。

发达的道路网络让日常生活更加便利。与此同时，该地区保留了传统文化和牧区生活方式，在传统与现代生活之间保持了良好平衡。中新社：今年是长征胜利90周年。为什么长征的故事继续在世界各地引起共鸣？韦尔登：我相信许多国家都经历过自己的“长征时刻”。在澳大利亚，一个例子是与加里波利战役相关的澳新军团精神。

从纯军事角度看，那场战役是一场失败。然而澳大利亚人继续纪念士兵们的勇气、他们在极其困难的情况下绝不放弃的精神以及他们照顾战友的承诺。这种精神与长征精神有共同之处。美国历史上还有另一个相似之处：美国独立战争期间大陆军在福吉谷的冬季营地。乔治·华盛顿的军队忍受了严寒、饥饿、疾病和反复的挫折。

它几乎瓦解。如果那个冬天摧毁了华盛顿的军队，美国历史的进程可能会完全不同。有许多这样的历史相似之处。各地人们都能理解的是一个在压倒性劣势中幸存下来的故事。这是人们在成功似乎不可能时继续前行的故事。

随着时间推移，对长征可能会有不同的解读，但历史事实依然存在：人们经历了非凡的磨难，他们所取得的成就塑造了中国的未来。即使在90年后，我仍然觉得长征令人鼓舞。它所代表的坚韧、团结和希望并不局限于一个国家。它们是人类共同精神遗产的一部分。从这个意义上说，每个国家都有自己的长征。

中新社：您多年从事跨文化交流。中澳两国人民在哪个层面最能产生共鸣？韦尔登：最能引起共鸣的通常是个人化的、与日常生活相关的事情。一个澳大利亚家庭希望自己的孩子生活得更好。一个中国家庭想要的完全一样。

那里没有地缘政治。这是一种共同的人类愿望。我参与了一个名为《中国一日》的摄影项目。来自世界各地的近100名摄影师被派往中国各地，记录同一天。这本书从午夜开始，到午夜结束。

读者可以看到农民在黎明时在小麦地里醒来，街头小贩在城市里工作，或者时装模特在上海参加拍摄。当这些场景放在一起时，人们会认识到，无论住在哪里，他们都有很多共同点。新闻报道往往集中于地缘政治、冲突、恐惧和不确定性。但相互理解和信任是通过普通人的真实生活建立起来的。这就是为什么社区层面和家庭层面的联系如此重要。

人文交流也必须超越口号。它不仅仅是观看太极拳表演或舞龙。它意味着人们一起工作、一起吃饭、一起做音乐、一起学习和创造。当人们真正参与彼此的生活时，文化交流才有意义。中新社：除了长征，您还对中国的哪些故事感兴趣？

韦尔登：我一直对中国的创新感兴趣。西方有些人曾把中国仅仅视为“模仿者”，但我从未同意这种观点。中国历史上产生过重要发明。今天，中国在电动汽车和人工智能等领域展现出强大的创新能力。我希望更多关于这种创新的故事能传达给国际受众。

与此同时，文化项目仍然是我最大的兴趣。我对三种跨文化故事特别感兴趣。第一种是关于在中国的澳大利亚人。一个例子是乔治·欧内斯特·莫理循，这位澳大利亚记者被称为“北京的莫理循”。第二种是关于在澳大利亚的中国人。淘金热时期中国移民的历史包含许多非凡的故事。

第三个领域是澳大利亚社会的日常现实。我希望中国受众看到更多关于澳大利亚人实际生活方式的、信息丰富且细致入微的故事。这些跨文化故事中有许多尚未被充分讲述。我希望继续充当桥梁，帮助澳大利亚人和中国人看到彼此更真实、更复杂、更人性化的一面。（完）他是一位澳大利亚汉学家、纪录片制片人、作家、主持人和摄影师，在澳中文化媒体和双边关系方面拥有41年经验。

他是中国事务特别顾问，曾获皮博迪奖和中国国家图书奖，并曾是澳中理事会成员。

articles.summaryCn: 中国通过一体化生态修复、科学干预与国际合作，推动生态系统恢复，为全球生物多样性保护提供实践范例。

paragraphs.en: Editor's note: As the UN {{22}} conference, COP17, calls for turning global commitments into action, {{23}} {{21}} is key to protecting biodiversity and strengthening ecological {{0}}. CGTN invites Zhang Zhenming, professor and vice dean of the School of Ecology and Nature Conservation under Beijing Forestry University, and associate professors Liu Jiakai and Ning Zhonghua from the same school to examine China's {{1}} approach to ecological restoration, its efforts to combine targeted {{2}} with natural recovery, and its contributions to global biodiversity {{20}} through international {{25}}. The article reflects the authors' opinions, and not necessarily those of CGTN. The UN biodiversity conference, COP17, marks the first major checkpoint to evaluate how countries have moved from biodiversity pledges to practice – exactly what the theme, "Taking Action for Nature," calls for. For China, the results are already in the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 编者按：随着联合国生物多样性大会COP17呼吁将全球承诺转化为行动，生态系统恢复成为保护生物多样性和增强生态韧性的关键。CGTN邀请北京林业大学生态与自然保护学院教授兼副院长张振明，以及同校副教授刘佳凯和宁中华，探讨中国生态修复的综合方法、将针对性干预与自然恢复相结合的努力，以及通过国际合作对全球生物多样性保护的贡献。本文仅代表作者观点，不一定代表CGTN立场。联合国生物多样性大会COP17是评估各国如何从生物多样性承诺转向实践的首个重要检查点——这正是“为自然采取行动”主题所呼吁的。对中国而言，成果已经落地。

paragraphs.en: Its ecological restoration methods offer a model for this effort: bringing connected landscapes under {{3}} management, strengthening nature's {{17}} to recover, and sharing knowledge through international cooperation. Over several decades, China has expanded forest resources, advanced grassland restoration, strengthened wetland protection and fought {{4}}. These efforts have contributed to global greening and improved soil conservation and carbon {{5}}. They have also shaped an approach that treats nature as a unified web, not isolated patches. At its heart is the idea that mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts form an {{6}} community of life.
paragraphs.cn: 其生态修复方法为这一努力提供了模式：将相连的景观纳入协调管理，增强自然的恢复能力，并通过国际合作分享知识。几十年来，中国扩大了森林资源，推进了草原恢复，加强了湿地保护并抗击了荒漠化。这些努力为全球绿化做出了贡献，并改善了土壤保持和碳封存。它们还形成了一种将自然视为统一网络而非孤立斑块的方法。其核心思想是，山水林田湖草沙构成一个相互联系的生命共同体。

paragraphs.en:
Restoration is planned at the river basin and landscape scale, taking account of water and soil resources and drawing on cooperation across regions and government departments. In the headwaters of the Oujiang River in east China's Zhejiang Province, restoring terraces alongside traditional farming connects mountain conservation with agricultural production. Editor's note: As the UN biodiversity conference, COP17, calls for turning global commitments into action, ecosystem restoration is key to protecting biodiversity and strengthening ecological resilience. CGTN invites Zhang Zhenming, professor and vice dean of the School of Ecology and Nature Conservation under Beijing Forestry University, and associate professors Liu Jiakai and Ning Zhonghua from the same school to examine China's integrated approach to ecological restoration, its efforts to combine targeted intervention with natural recovery, and its contributions to global biodiversity conservation through international cooperation. The article reflects the authors' opinions, and not necessarily those of CGTN.
The UN biodiversity conference, COP17, marks the first major checkpoint to evaluate how countries have moved from biodiversity pledges to practice – exactly what the theme, "Taking Action for Nature," calls for.
For China, the results are already in the ground. Its ecological restoration methods offer a model for this effort: bringing connected landscapes under coordinated management, strengthening nature's capacity to recover, and sharing knowledge through international cooperation.
Over several decades, China has expanded forest resources, advanced grassland restoration, strengthened wetland protection and fought desertification. These efforts have contributed to global greening and improved soil conservation and carbon sequestration. They have also shaped an approach that treats nature as a unified web, not isolated patches.
At its heart is the idea that mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts form an interconnected community of life. Restoration is planned at the river basin and landscape scale, taking account of water and soil resources and drawing on cooperation across regions and government departments.
Water flows, sediment and nutrients move, and animals migrate – all of which link habitats. Planning around these connections helps local projects support the functioning of a wider region, bringing land use decisions and the recovery of ecological processes into a common framework.
Working with nature
In the headwaters of the Oujiang River in east China's Zhejiang Province, restoring terraces alongside traditional farming connects mountain conservation with agricultural production. In the Yellow River Delta, controlling invasive plants and reopening tidal channels creates conditions for native species to recover. Both examples show how practical interventions can work with natural processes.
The Three-North Shelterbelt Forest Program illustrates the value of continuity. Through long-term planning, it brings sand control, water management and land restoration into a sustained effort. Together, landscape planning, continued investment and locally tailored measures tie individual projects to regional conservation goals.
Wetland conservation at Namtso in Xizang Autonomous Region, southwest China. /Liu Jiakai
Minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery
As restoration advances, greater emphasis is being placed on ecosystem quality, ecological integrity and lasting resilience. Climate change, extreme weather and human activity continue to alter the conditions for recovery. Biodiversity conservation, ecosystem functions and the capacity for self-renewal must be addressed together, so restored ecosystems can adapt, withstand disturbance and continue providing services.
This calls for combining targeted intervention with natural recovery. Our team has proposed an approach we call "minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery." It explores how identifying key barriers to recovery and intervening at the right places, at the right times and with appropriate intensity can help ecosystems regain their capacity to organize and repair themselves.
Putting these ideas into practice requires integrated observation, research into ecological mechanisms and ongoing evaluation. Restoration planning should account for water availability and soil conditions, keeping interventions within local ecological limits. Cooperation across regions, sustained funding and long-term stewardship can connect scientific research with implementation and adaptive management, allowing measures to change as ecosystems respond.
Native Suaeda salsa restoration at a site where the invasive Spartina alterniflora has been removed, Yellow River Estuary, Dongying, Shandong Province, east China. /Ning Zhonghua
Sharing the playbook
China also contributes to global conservation through practical experience, joint research and capacity building. The Shan-Shui Initiative, recognized among the UN's first World Restoration Flagships, offers lessons in coordinating large-scale restoration over the long term.
Along China's Yellow Sea and Bohai Gulf coast, World Heritage wetlands connect local habitat management with conservation across the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. At Tiaozini in Yancheng, east China's Jiangsu Province, the managed "720" high-tide roost gives waterbirds a place to rest when rising tides cover their feeding grounds. Protecting such sites helps sustain a migration route extending far beyond China's borders.
In Mauritania, where straw is scarce, Chinese researchers and local partners adapted sand stabilization techniques to local conditions, combining nylon sand barriers with water-saving irrigation and training in maintenance and operation. Sharing technical knowledge alongside practical skills helps build the capacity to sustain the work. The value lies in developing solutions with local partners and equipping them to manage those solutions over time.
The International Mangrove Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, provides another platform for research exchanges and international training, supporting cooperation on coastal ecosystem conservation and restoration.
Such partnerships bring experience from different regions into shared efforts to protect biodiversity. They also create opportunities to compare methods and learn how different landscapes respond to restoration.
China exchanges ideas and practical approaches at meetings of the wetlands and biodiversity conventions, as well as the Global Ecological Governance (Nansen) Conference, Asia Philanthropy Forum and Zhongguancun Forum. The Flyway University Alliance extends these exchanges into collaborative research, monitoring and training. Chinese youth representatives have also brought stories of conservation on the ground to the global stage.
These efforts give practical meaning to COP17's call for action. By connecting integrated restoration, scientific inquiry and international cooperation, China can contribute to lasting biodiversity gains and stronger ecosystem functions, while helping develop approaches suited to different environments and needs.

articles.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's visit to China highlights the importance of dialogue, mutual trust and shared economic interests in advancing bilateral ties. articles.summaryCn: 德国总统施泰因迈尔时隔近八年访华，旨在巩固互信、深化合作，推动中德及中欧关系稳定发展。

paragraphs.en: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier delivers a keynote address at the German Environmental Award ceremony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, October 25, 2026. Nearly eight years after his last visit, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier will return to China on Tuesday for a six-day state visit. According to the German presidency, Steinmeier will begin his trip in east China's Anhui Province, visiting a traditional village to learn about the country's rural history and Volkswagen China Technology Company in Hefei. He will then travel to Beijing for formal talks at the Great Hall of the People and meet students at Peking University. China's Foreign Ministry said Beijing hopes to use the visit to {{0}} mutual trust, deepen cooperation and pursue joint {{2}}, advancing {{1}} relations and contributing to the steady development of China-Europe ties.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年10月25日，德国总统弗兰克-瓦尔特·施泰因迈尔在德国北莱茵-威斯特法伦州举行的德国环境奖颁奖典礼上发表主旨演讲。时隔近八年，德国总统弗兰克-瓦尔特·施泰因迈尔将于周二重返中国，进行为期六天的国事访问。据德国总统府称，施泰因迈尔将首先访问中国东部的安徽省，参观一个传统村落以了解该国的乡村历史，并访问位于合肥的大众汽车中国技术公司。随后他将前往北京，在人民大会堂举行正式会谈，并在北京大学与学生会面。中国外交部表示，北京希望利用此次访问巩固互信、深化合作、追求共同创新，推进双边关系，并为中欧关系的稳定发展作出贡献。

paragraphs.en:
Dialogue and cooperation: Building on shared interests
Volkswagen's presence in Hefei offers a concrete example of how China-Germany cooperation is evolving. The city hosts the automaker's largest global software research and development center for intelligent connected vehicles outside its headquarters in Wolfsburg, Germany, reflecting the role of China's innovation {{3}} in the company's global development. The economic links between the two countries have long been visible in everyday business. Speaking at the Hamburg Summit in November 2016, when he was Germany's foreign minister, Steinmeier noted that nearly one in three containers unloaded at the Port of Hamburg came from China, while one in five Airbus aircraft assembled at Hamburg's Finkenwerder facility went to Chinese buyers. He cited these examples to illustrate the depth of bilateral economic ties and emphasized the importance of {{4}} and open dialogue in addressing differences and sustaining cooperation.
paragraphs.cn:

China on Monday issued a guideline to boost financial support for building international science and technology centers in Beijing (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region), Shanghai (the Yangtze River Delta), and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA).
The guideline, released by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) along with ten other departments, aims to build a financial service system that better matches the core functions and international positioning of the three innovation hubs.
By 2030, the country aims to establish a sound full-chain financial service system for technological innovation, achieve a "notable increase" in the proportion of direct financing, and basically form a pattern of integrated financial services in the three regions, according to the guideline.
Among the specific measures, the guideline calls for improving foreign exchange business facilitation policies for qualified foreign limited partners (QFLP), a move that is expected to facilitate overseas institutions' equity investment in China.
It also vows to make cross-border fund management simpler for multinational tech companies and for Chinese firms funding their overseas R&D centers.
The document sets out differentiated priorities for each region. The Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region will focus on original innovation and coordinated regional innovation, with stronger financial support for major science and technology infrastructure.
The Yangtze River Delta will leverage its industrial cluster advantages to build a technology finance ecosystem featuring multi-party participation and shared benefits.
The GBA will develop an open technology finance system, with an emphasis on deepening high-level financial interaction and regulatory alignment among Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao.
The guideline also stresses building risk prevention and control mechanisms to firmly guard against systemic financial risks.
Speaking at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026 in Beijing on Monday, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said that building the three international sci-tech innovation centers is a major strategy of the central authorities. Pan highlighted that the central bank will push for greater pilot efforts in the three regions in areas such as relending, the bond market's "sci-tech board" and cross-border investment and financing.
The country's 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-2025) called for supporting the initiative of making Beijing, Shanghai, and the GBA international centers for science and technology innovation, a goal that has guided progress over the past five years.
The expansion of the Beijing and Shanghai centers into the wider Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and the Yangtze River Delta, respectively, marks a shift from single-city breakthroughs toward coordinated regional development, a direction set out at the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference.

An embodied intelligence robot sorts packages in the service robot zone at the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, October 15, 2026. 
The offline exhibition of the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, is underway, attracting large numbers of buyers from around the world. With a focus on innovation and digital intelligence, the fair showcases a wide range of AI-powered products, as emerging technologies and applications help drive industrial upgrading and support foreign trade growth.
Cutting-edge products on display include AI-powered humanoid robots and industrial robotic arms, autonomous window-cleaning robots, multilingual translation glasses and AI earphones. Through live demonstrations and interactive experiences, exhibitors are showcasing the latest technological breakthroughs and their practical applications.
AI-powered products bring innovation to life
Smart glasses equipped with AI can identify objects and provide relevant information through voice commands. One model on display allows users to check the estimated calorie content of food and receive low-calorie meal recommendations through a connected mobile application.
An overseas buyer tries out smart glasses in the service robot zone at the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, October 17, 2026. 
Health wearables are also evolving, with screenless smart bands and smart rings offering compact alternatives to conventional devices. Some can operate for one to two weeks on a single charge, while their companion apps generate AI-powered health reports and offer personalized health management recommendations.
AI earphones are designed to improve speech recognition in noisy environments, facilitating smoother cross-language communication. Exhibitors said continued research and development had improved sound pickup, helping maintain recognition quality even in the crowded exhibition venue.
An overseas buyer interacts with a robot during the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, October 15, 2026. 
The fair is showcasing 235,000 AI products, while more than 20,000 participating enterprises have adopted new technologies and business models, including industrial internet and AI. Exhibitors are focusing on turning technological advances into practical applications and bringing research achievements to market.
In the home appliance section, companies are integrating AI into a range of household settings, including living rooms, kitchens and laundry areas. Rather than focusing solely on individual appliances, exhibitors are offering integrated smart home solutions designed to address everyday needs, attracting considerable interest from overseas buyers.
